_comment: Living taste profile for the wine-buying skill. Grows as verdicts get logged in cellar.jsonl. likes/dislikes are style-level signals; benchmarks are named reference bottles; notes is free-text. Edit by hand or let the buying/feedback skills append.
likes: Savory Left Bank Graves / Pessac-Leognan reds (Cab Sauv + Merlot on gravel): supple, silky, and with a 30-45 min decant a lovely floral perfume that carries into a cohesive palate. Integrated mineral bitterness is a PLUS here.
Plush, fruit-forward Right Bank Merlot (velvety black cherry/plum, cocoa, easy roundness) — tasty and crowd-friendly.
dislikes: UNINTEGRATED bitterness: a true-bitter 'bitter-almond' spike on the finish that sits disjointed over a lighter mid-palate/body (limestone Right Bank signature — St-Emilion, Lalande-de-Pomerol, Fronsac, Castillon; amplified by Cabernet Franc). NOTE: bitterness itself is not the problem — see the Rochemorin like below. The problem is bitterness that clashes rather than integrates.
benchmarks: Chateau de Rochemorin 2019 (Pessac-Leognan) = LOVE. The good version of the bitterness axis: floral perfume + supple/silky texture + mineral bitterness that is integrated and cohesive. Reference for 'bitterness done right'. Decant 30-45 min to unlock the perfume.

Chateau Garraud 2019 (Lalande-de-Pomerol) = LIKE. The cautionary version: tasty but the bitter-almond finish was jarring/disjointed against a lighter body. Reference for the bitterness that does NOT work.
notes: KEY TASTE AXIS (bitterness): the deciding factor is INTEGRATION + cohesion, not the presence of bitterness. Bitterness works when the wine is supple/silky with enough mid-palate weight, perfume, and cohesion to carry it (Rochemorin, love); it fails when it's a bitter-almond spike over a lighter, disjointed frame (Garraud, like-but-flawed). Buying implications: (1) A decant of 30-45 min matters — it unlocked the Rochemorin's perfume from a tight start. (2) For Right Bank, favor clay/gravel/iron (Pomerol) over limestone-plateau St-Emilion/satellites, AND favor bottles with enough weight/cohesion to carry the finish. (3) Savory Left Bank Graves/Pessac-Leognan is a confirmed sweet spot. Verdicts logged so far: Rochemorin 2019 (love), Garraud 2019 (like).
